title: rollback-checkpoint-manifest-prototype
content:
Purpose:
Small, focused sketch for a compact checkpoint manifest format that supports efficient rollback and fast delta application for client-side session offload. Target usage: lightweight session offload from edge clients to cache nodes or S3-like object store; must support range-based retrieval, integrity verification, and cheap tombstone/rollback semantics.

Goals:
- Single compact manifest per checkpoint bundle that enumerates blobs and lightweight lineage info.
- Support both full restore and incremental apply (patching).
- Enable cryptographic integrity checks (sha256 or blake3) per blob and a manifest-level Merkle root.
- Make rollbacks cheap: manifest encodes ancestor pointers + applied-delta tree so we can compute minimal revert set.
- Keep on-wire shape small (aim <= 2KB for typical short session bundles).

Constraints / assumptions:
- Clients are resource-constrained (mobile/edge) so server does heavy lifting (compute diffs, create patches).
- Storage backends may have object size limits; prefer many small blobs rather than a single monolithic bundle.
- Network: occasional high-latency links, need resumable downloads.
- Must interop with existing prefix/KV caching and session snapshot formats.

High-level idea (human):
- Each checkpoint bundle = manifest.json + blobs/ (KV entries, context-blob, kv-index).
- Manifest lists entries with (key, blob_id, size, checksum, type, optional-range) and a per-bundle merkle root computed over ordered blob_id list.
- For incremental pushes, server stores "delta manifests" that reference base manifest id + list of add/remove/patch ops; patch ops point to patch-blob which is an ordered delta for target blob.
- Rollback: client can provide a previous manifest id; server computes revert manifest = inverse ops. If server cannot compute inverse cheaply, it returns list of blobs to reapply from ancestor.

Manifest example (concrete shape for implementation):
- top-level keys: bundle_id, created_at, base_manifest_id (nullable), merkle_root, blobs: [list], ops: [list optional], meta: { string tags }
(embedding as JSON here for clarity)

{
  "bundle_id": "bundle_20250214_007e9",
  "created_at": "2025-02-14T11:22:33Z",
  "base_manifest_id": "bundle_20250213_f3a2",
  "merkle_root": "b5f8c3...",
  "blobs": [
    {"key": "kv/user:12345/context", "blob_id": "obj_001", "size": 4096, "checksum": "sha256:...", "type": "context"},
    {"key": "kv/user:12345/kv-index", "blob_id": "obj_002", "size": 512, "checksum": "sha256:...", "type": "index"}
  ],
  "ops": [
    {"op": "add", "key": "kv/user:12345/new", "blob_id": "obj_003"},
    {"op": "patch", "key": "kv/user:12345/context", "patch_blob_id": "obj_004", "desc": "delta from obj_000 -> obj_001"},
    {"op": "remove", "key": "kv/user:12345/old"}
  ],
  "meta": {"client_version":"0.9.1", "origin":"edge-proxy"}
}

Notes about fields:
- base_manifest_id: null for full checkpoints. For incremental checkpoints this links to the manifest used as base to compute ops. We allow chains but encourage server-side compaction.
- merkle_root: computed over ordered blob_id byte sequences. This lets clients verify integrity with O(log N) proofs when server provides merkle proofs.
- blobs[].type enum: context | index | kv | patch | tombstone | metadata.
- ops[] are applied in listed order to move from base_manifest -> current. ops provide revertibility if we record inverse ops (or we compute inverse during rollback on server and return a revert-manifest).

Merkle / integrity model:
- Use Blake3-256 for speed on mobile; fallback to sha256 for longer-lived artifacts.
- Server stores per-blob checksums and merkle tree. Clients can request a subset proof: request merkle proof for blob_id(s) and server returns siblings.
- For resume: blobs support ranged GETs and we include optional byte ranges in manifest (start/length).

Delta / patch model:
- Patch blob is a compact edit script (simple: bsdiff-style or custom TLV of (copy, insert) ops).
- Server computes patch between base blob and new blob; patch is stored as separate blob with type=patch and referenced in ops[].
- Client apply sequence: fetch patch blob, fetch base blob (if not cached), apply patch -> verify checksum -> swap into place. If base blob missing, client requests server to provide reconstructed full blob (server may respond with full blob_id).

Rollback workflow (client-initiated):
1) Client asks storage node: "revert to manifest_id=X".
2) Storage node computes revert manifest: if current manifest has base_manifest_id chain and ops are reversible, node emits inverse ops in revert-manifest. If ops not reversible (e.g., tombstone permanently deleted), node signals need_full_restore=true and provides list of blobs to fetch.
3) Client applies revert-manifest ops in order (or requests full manifest restoration).

API prototypes (HTTP/JSON):
- POST /v1/checkpoints/upload-manifest -> {bundle_id, manifest_url}  (server validates merkle + checksums)
- GET /v1/checkpoints/{bundle_id}/manifest -> returns manifest JSON + headers (ETag=merkle_root)
- POST /v1/checkpoints/{bundle_id}/revert -> body {target_manifest_id: string} -> returns {revert_manifest_id, ops=[...], need_full_restore: bool}
- GET /v1/checkpoints/{bundle_id}/blob/{blob_id}?range=0-1023 -> returns blob bytes (supports range)
Resumability / partial fetch patterns:
- Clients can do 1) fetch manifest, 2) compute list of missing blob_ids vs local cache, 3) call batch GET /v1/checkpoints/{bundle_id}/blobs?ids=obj_001,obj_002 -> server streams blobs in tar-like multipart with per-part checksum. For high-latency, allow chunked multipart and re-attach.

Eviction and tombstones:
- When a blob is removed via op remove/tombstone, manifest records tombstone with tombstone_id and optional retention TTL (eg 7d) for fast undelete during short rollbacks.
- For long-term GC, server compacts manifests into milestones and prunes intermediate blobs: clients can request nearest milestone for restore.

Compatibility notes with KV caching and prefix caching:
- Blob keys align with existing kv namespace: e.g., kv/user:ID/..., so cache shards can route by prefix.
- Manifest-level merkle proofs can be produced by cache nodes without fetching all blobs; they only need per-blob checksums + tree metadata.

Open questions / TODOs (actionable):
- Q1: Do we store patch deltas server-side indefinitely or GC them after X days? (tradeoff: storage vs rollback window).
- Q2: What is expected average manifest size? If too big we should compress header and use binary manifest.
- Q3: How to handle partial blob corruption mid-download? Proposal: server returns chunk-level checksums and clients verify incremental.
- TODO: write unit test harness for merkle proof verification (RI-4521). (owner: Aisha).
- TODO: prototype bsdiff-based patching in go runtime and measure CPU on mobile builds (Tomás).

Other notes / sketches:
- ASCII sketch: manifest -> blobs stored across object-store and cache nodes:

   client                              cache node                             object store
      |  POST manifest ----------------->| validate merkle -> store meta        |
      |  fetch missing blobs ------------>| check local cache -> 200 stream    |
      |                                   | if miss -> fetch from object store  |

- Fast revert optimization: keep a short (N=3) ring of recent manifests per bundle id in cache nodes so small backsteps do not require full recreation.

Back-of-envelope: estimate sizes:
- typical short session: 6 blobs (context 4KB + 4 small kvs 512B each + index 256B) -> manifest JSON ~650 bytes; with merkle and ops ~850B. Good target.

References / links: see linked_artifacts.

If we converge on this shape, next steps:
- finalize proto shape and produce protobuf/avro schema for compactness.
- implement server-side generator that computes ops and merkle proofs.
- implement go client small library for apply/rollback with tests.

Notes-to-self: keep manifest fields stable; avoid renaming merkle_root -> rootHash later (breaks proof clients).

End of sketch.
